chapter_seo_title: The Starseizing Hand Unleashed - Ji Ning's Rescue Mission - Chapter 429 of Desolate Era
chapter_meta_description: Ji Ning rescues his brother and unleashes the full fury of the Starseizing Hand, dismantling an enemy stronghold to face a terrifying silver-armored general in this epic chapter.
og_description: Watch Ji Ning execute his vengeance with surgical precision and the overwhelming power of the Starseizing Hand.
twitter_title: Ji Ning's palm is mightier than the sword!
twitter_description: A rescue mission turns into a systematic slaughter as Ji Ning unveils the true power of his divine ability.

lore_anchors.definition: A one-time-use talisman that allows a cultivator to instantly teleport across vast distances, capable of bypassing many spatial defenses.
A top-ten divine ability of the Three Realms that transforms the user's hands into weapons of immense power, capable of crushing worlds at its highest level.
A Fiendgod Body Refining cultivator at the Void stage, possessing a powerful, near-indestructible divine body and immense strength.
A category of magic treasure above Immortal-rank, possessing incredible power and a nascent spiritual nature.
The full-scale version of the Lesser Thousand Sword Formation, capable of coordinating hundreds of flying swords for devastating attacks and defense.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why doesn't Ji Ning just use his swords against the Void Fiendgod?
cultural_notes_faq.a: He uses his palms not as a default, but to test the full power of the Starseizing Hand now that his identity is exposed, and to prove that a Sword Immortal can use any part of his body as a sword.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Is the silver-armored youth as strong as Ji Ning?
cultural_notes_faq.a: The collision of his arrow and the Grand Thousand Sword Formation was a draw, suggesting they are closely matched for now, but the battle is just beginning.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why did Ji Ning attack the fleeing Loose Immortals?
cultural_notes_faq.a: He made a silent, visceral vow to avenge Mu Northson's suffering. To him, everyone in this stronghold who participated in harming his brother is guilty and deserving of death.
